label: Matt 23:1
text: Then Jesus spoke to the multitudes and to his disciples,

label: Matt 23:2
text:
saying,
“The scribes and the Pharisees sat on Moses’ seat.

label: Matt 23:3
text: All things therefore whatever they tell you to observe, observe and do, but don’t do their works; for they say, and don’t do.

label: Matt 23:4
text: For they bind heavy burdens that are grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not lift a finger to help them.

label: Matt 23:5
text:
But all their works they do to be seen by men. They make their phylacteries

broad, enlarge the fringes
of their garments,

label: Matt 23:6
text: and love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues,

label: Matt 23:7
text: the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called ‘Rabbi, Rabbi’ by men.

label: Matt 23:8
text: But don’t you be called ‘Rabbi,’ for one is your teacher, the Christ, and all of you are brothers.

label: Matt 23:9
text: Call no man on the earth your father, for one is your Father, he who is in heaven.

label: Matt 23:10
text: Neither be called masters, for one is your master, the Christ.

label: Matt 23:11
text: But he who is greatest among you will be your servant.

label: Matt 23:12
text: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

label: Matt 23:13
text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows’ houses, and as a pretense you make long prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.

label: Matt 23:14
text: “But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you shut up the Kingdom of Heaven against men; for you don’t enter in yourselves, neither do you allow those who are entering in to enter.

variants.reading: the verse is absent (13 'Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!' is followed by 15 'Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land...')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'List of omitted Bible verses' (s.v. Matthew 23:14): the verse is 'lacking altogether in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus, Codex Bezae, Codex Regius, Codex Dublinensis, Codex Koridethi, Family 1, Ethiopic, Armenian, several Italic, Syrian, and Coptic manuscripts'; it appears before verse 13 in Codex Cyprius and Codex Washingtonianus and after verse 13 in Family 13; Bruce Metzger: 'There can be little doubt that the words [...] are spurious here', borrowed from the parallel Mark 12:40/Luke 20:47. The World English Bible includes the verse.

label: Matt 23:15
text:
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna
as yourselves.

label: Matt 23:16
text: “Woe to you, you blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple, he is obligated.’

label: Matt 23:17
text: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold?

label: Matt 23:18
text: ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it, he is obligated?’

label: Matt 23:19
text: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?

label: Matt 23:20
text: He therefore who swears by the altar, swears by it, and by everything on it.

label: Matt 23:21
text:
He who swears by the temple, swears by it, and by him who has been living
in it.

label: Matt 23:22
text: He who swears by heaven, swears by the throne of God, and by him who sits on it.

label: Matt 23:23
text:
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin,
and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But you ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.

label: Matt 23:24
text: You blind guides, who strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel!

label: Matt 23:25
text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and unrighteousness.

label: Matt 23:26
text: You blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and of the platter, that its outside may become clean also.

label: Matt 23:27
text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.

label: Matt 23:28
text: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

label: Matt 23:29
text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and decorate the tombs of the righteous,

label: Matt 23:30
text: and say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we wouldn’t have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.’

label: Matt 23:31
text: Therefore you testify to yourselves that you are children of those who killed the prophets.

label: Matt 23:32
text: Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers.

label: Matt 23:33
text: You serpents, you offspring of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?

label: Matt 23:34
text: Therefore behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify; and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues, and persecute from city to city;

label: Matt 23:35
text: that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.

label: Matt 23:36
text: Most certainly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.

label: Matt 23:37
text: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets, and stones those who are sent to her! How often I would have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!

label: Matt 23:38
text: Behold, your house is left to you desolate.

label: Matt 23:39
text: For I tell you, you will not see me from now on, until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”

label: The scribes and Pharisees sit on Moses' seat
statement: The scribes and the Pharisees sat on Moses' seat - a recognized seat or office of teaching authority in the synagogue setting.

label: They make their phylacteries broad
statement: The scribes and Pharisees wear phylacteries (tefillin) and make them broad to be seen by men.

label: They enlarge the fringes of their garments
statement: The scribes and Pharisees wear fringes (tzitzit) on their garments and enlarge them to be seen by men.

label: Places of honor at feasts and best seats in the synagogues
statement: The scribes and Pharisees love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues, and the salutations in the marketplaces.

label: They love to be called 'Rabbi'
statement: The scribes and Pharisees love to be called 'Rabbi, Rabbi' by men; Jesus tells his disciples not to be called Rabbi, for one is their teacher.

label: They travel sea and land to make one proselyte
statement: The scribes and Pharisees travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one they make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as themselves.

label: A hierarchy of oaths by the temple, its gold, the altar and heaven
statement: The blind guides teach that whoever swears by the temple it is nothing, but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is obligated - likewise the altar and its gift; Jesus ranks the temple, the altar and heaven above gold, gift and throne.

label: They tithe mint, dill and cumin
statement: The scribes and Pharisees tithe mint, dill and cumin, while leaving undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy and faith.

label: They clean the outside of the cup and platter
statement: The scribes and Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and of the platter while the inside is full of extortion and unrighteousness; Jesus says first clean the inside, that the outside may become clean also.

label: Whitewashed tombs, beautiful outside, full of bones
statement: The scribes and Pharisees are like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful but inwardly are full of dead men's bones and all uncleanness.

label: They build and decorate the tombs of the prophets and righteous
statement: The scribes and Pharisees build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the tombs of the righteous, saying they would not have shared in their fathers' bloodshed.

label: Zechariah son of Barachiah killed between the sanctuary and the altar
statement: Zechariah son of Barachiah was killed between the sanctuary and the altar - the martyrdom that closes the list from righteous Abel.

label: Jerusalem kills the prophets; the house is left desolate
statement: Jesus laments that Jerusalem kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, and says 'Behold, your house is left to you desolate' (a prediction in the text; the Temple was destroyed in 70 CE).

label: They will not see him till they say 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord'
statement: Jesus says they will not see him from now on until they say 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord' - the acclamation of Psalm 118:26.
